speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity and maternal gestational diabetes.

The chest X-ray findings of a ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms, combined with respiratory acidosis on the arterial blood gas, are classic for surfactant deficiency. Given your history of being born at 32 weeks and your mother's gestational diabetes, this confirms the clinical picture of RDS. Is the baby currently on oxygen support or receiving surfactant therapy?
